recipes.name: Turkey & Egg Scramble with Toast
recipes.description: Your standard weekday breakfast: lean turkey scrambled with a whole egg, egg whites, spinach and peppers, with two slices of thin-sliced whole-grain toast.

ingredients.name: Ground turkey 93/7
ingredients.notes: 151 g raw ≈ 4 oz (113 g) cooked at a 75% yield assumption

ingredients.name: Dave's Killer Bread Thin-Sliced 21 Whole Grains

steps: Heat the oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-high. Add the turkey, break it up, and cook 6–7 minutes until no pink remains and it reaches 165°F / 74°C. Season with the salt, pepper and garlic powder.
Add the diced bell pepper and cook 2 minutes. Add the spinach and stir until just wilted, about 1 minute.
Whisk the whole egg into the egg whites, pour over the turkey mixture, and fold gently over medium-low heat 2–3 minutes until set with no liquid egg left.
Toast the two slices of bread and serve alongside.
storage: Cool quickly and refrigerate within 2 hours in shallow airtight containers.
Use refrigerated portions within 3–4 days. Freeze portions for days 4–5 on prep day and move them to the fridge the night before.
Reheat until steaming hot throughout (165°F / 74°C). Add a teaspoon of water over rice or pasta before microwaving, covered.
Ground turkey is done at 165°F / 74°C.

source.title: Tanner's usual breakfast
source.changes: Your own recipe as described: 4 oz cooked 93/7 turkey, 1 egg, ½ cup egg whites, 1 cup spinach, ½ cup bell pepper and 2 slices of Dave's Killer Bread Thin-Sliced 21 Whole Grains. Gather converts the turkey to a raw buying weight.

recipes.name: Egg & Egg-White Breakfast Sandwich
recipes.description: A whole egg whisked with egg whites, cooked into a folded patty, on two slices of thin-sliced whole-grain toast.

ingredients.name: Dave's Killer Bread Thin-Sliced 21 Whole Grains

steps: Whisk the whole egg into the egg whites with the salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-low. Pour in the egg mixture, let it set 1–2 minutes, then fold it into a square the size of the bread. Cook until no liquid egg remains.
Toast the bread and assemble the sandwich.

Use refrigerated portions within 3–4 days. Freeze portions for days 4–5 on prep day and move them to the fridge the night before.
Reheat until steaming hot throughout (165°F / 74°C). Add a teaspoon of water over rice or pasta before microwaving, covered.

recipes.name: Ginger-Soy Chicken Thighs with Snap Peas
recipes.description: Seared thighs glazed in a ginger, garlic and soy reduction, over jasmine rice with crisp sesame snap peas.
steps: Rinse the jasmine rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Combine with water (1¼ cups water per cup of dry rice) and the rice salt, bring to a boil, cover, and cook on low 15 minutes. Rest off the heat 10 minutes, then fluff.
Whisk the soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, ginger and garlic. Toss the thighs with half of it and marinate at least 20 minutes (up to overnight).
Sear the thighs in the avocado oil in a skillet over medium-high, 5–6 minutes per side, until 165°F / 74°C (closer to 175°F keeps thighs most tender).
Pour in the remaining sauce and simmer 1–2 minutes, turning the chicken to glaze. Rest 5 minutes, then slice.
Wipe the pan, stir-fry the snap peas 2–3 minutes until bright, and toss with the sesame oil.
Finish with green onion and sesame seeds.
storage: Cool quickly and refrigerate within 2 hours in shallow airtight containers.
Use refrigerated portions within 3–4 days. Freeze portions for days 4–5 on prep day and move them to the fridge the night before.
Reheat until steaming hot throughout (165°F / 74°C). Add a teaspoon of water over rice or pasta before microwaving, covered.
Chicken is done at 165°F / 74°C in the thickest part.

source.title: Ginger-Soy Sauce Chicken
source.changes: Uses boneless skinless thighs pan-seared instead of roasted whole pieces, a measured per-serving glaze, and adds snap peas and jasmine rice for a prep bowl.

recipes.name: Teriyaki Chicken Broccoli Bowls
recipes.description: Diced chicken breast in a from-scratch teriyaki (soy, honey, ginger, garlic) with steamed broccoli and jasmine rice.

ingredients.name: Cornstarch
ingredients.notes: whisked with 1 tbsp water per serving

steps: Rinse the jasmine rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Combine with water (1¼ cups water per cup of dry rice) and the rice salt, bring to a boil, cover, and cook on low 15 minutes. Rest off the heat 10 minutes, then fluff.
Whisk the soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, garlic, ginger and the cornstarch slurry into a teriyaki sauce.
Brown the chicken in the oil over medium-high, 6–8 minutes, until 165°F / 74°C.
Pour in the sauce and simmer 1–2 minutes until glossy and thick.
Steam the broccoli 4–5 minutes until bright and just tender. Spread on a tray to cool so they stay crisp in the container.
Pack rice, broccoli and chicken; spoon pan sauce over the chicken and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
storage: Cool quickly and refrigerate within 2 hours in shallow airtight containers.
Use refrigerated portions within 3–4 days. Freeze portions for days 4–5 on prep day and move them to the fridge the night before.
Reheat until steaming hot throughout (165°F / 74°C). Add a teaspoon of water over rice or pasta before microwaving, covered.
Chicken is done at 165°F / 74°C in the thickest part.

recipes.name: Gochujang Beef Rice Bowls
recipes.description: 93/7 beef cooked with gochujang, garlic, ginger and soy, served over rice with quick-pickled cucumber and shredded carrot.
steps: Rinse the jasmine rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Combine with water (1¼ cups water per cup of dry rice) and the rice salt, bring to a boil, cover, and cook on low 15 minutes. Rest off the heat 10 minutes, then fluff.
Toss the cucumber with the rice vinegar and a pinch of salt; let it sit while you cook.
Brown the beef in a skillet over medium-high, 6–7 minutes, breaking it up, until 160°F / 71°C. Drain any excess fat.
Add garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, then stir in the gochujang, soy sauce and honey and cook 1–2 minutes until glossy. Finish with sesame oil.
Pack rice, beef, cucumbers and carrots; top with green onion and sesame seeds.
storage: Cool quickly and refrigerate within 2 hours in shallow airtight containers.
Use refrigerated portions within 3–4 days. Freeze portions for days 4–5 on prep day and move them to the fridge the night before.
Reheat until steaming hot throughout (165°F / 74°C). Add a teaspoon of water over rice or pasta before microwaving, covered.

recipes.name: Sesame-Ginger Turkey & Green Bean Bowls

Return the green beans, toss, and finish with green onion and sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Honey-Garlic Chicken with Roasted Carrots
recipes.description: Sheet-pan thighs brushed with a honey-garlic-soy glaze, roasted alongside carrots and baby potatoes.

ingredients.name: Olive oil
ingredients.notes: for the glaze; for the carrots; for the potatoes

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.notes: for the carrots; for the potatoes

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the potato pieces with the potato oil, salt, black pepper and garlic powder. Roast on a sheet pan 30–35 minutes, flipping once, until browned and fork-tender.
Whisk the honey, soy sauce, garlic, glaze oil and pepper.
After the potatoes have roasted 10 minutes, add the carrots (tossed in their oil and salt) and the thighs to the pan. Brush the thighs with half the glaze.
Roast 20–25 minutes more, brushing with the rest of the glaze halfway, until the chicken reaches 165°F / 74°C and the carrots are tender.
Scatter with parsley.
storage: Cool quickly and refrigerate within 2 hours in shallow airtight containers.
Use refrigerated portions within 3–4 days. Freeze portions for days 4–5 on prep day and move them to the fridge the night before.
Reheat until steaming hot throughout (165°F / 74°C). Add a teaspoon of water over rice or pasta before microwaving, covered.

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.notes: for the broccoli; for the rice water

recipes.name: Japanese-Style Grilled Chicken (Yakitori Tare)
recipes.description: Thigh pieces grilled or broiled with a reduced soy-mirin tare, with a crunchy cabbage slaw and rice.
steps: Rinse the jasmine rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Combine with water (1¼ cups water per cup of dry rice) and the rice salt, bring to a boil, cover, and cook on low 15 minutes. Rest off the heat 10 minutes, then fluff.

Thread the chicken and green onion pieces onto skewers (or spread on a foil-lined sheet pan) and brush with the oil.
Grill over medium-high or broil 6 inches from the element 10–12 minutes, turning and brushing with tare in the last 4 minutes, until 165°F / 74°C.
Toss the cabbage with the rice vinegar, sesame oil and sesame seeds.
Pack rice, slaw and chicken; drizzle the reserved tare over the chicken.
storage: Cool quickly and refrigerate within 2 hours in shallow airtight containers.

recipes.description: Lightly cornstarch-coated chicken crisped in the air fryer and tossed in a fresh orange-ginger sauce, with broccoli and rice.

ingredients.name: Cornstarch
ingredients.notes: 8 g to coat, 2 g for the sauce

recipes.name: Chipotle-Adobo Chicken Thigh Rice Bowls with Broccoli
recipes.description: Chipotle-adobo marinated chicken thighs air-fried and served over jasmine rice with roasted broccoli, salsa and lime.
steps: Mash the chipotle with minced garlic, cumin, oregano, salt, half the oil and half the lime juice. Coat the thighs and marinate at least 30 minutes (up to overnight).
Cook the rice. Heat the air fryer to 400°F / 200°C.
Air-fry the thighs 14–15 minutes, flipping halfway, until 175°F / 80°C inside. Toss the broccoli with the remaining oil and salt and add it for the last 8 minutes.
Rest the chicken 5 minutes and slice. Serve over rice with broccoli, salsa, cilantro and the rest of the lime.
storage: Best eaten fresh the night you cook it.
If anything is left, refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 2 days. Reheat to 165°F / 74°C.

source.title: Chipotle Chicken
source.changes: Portioned per person with rice, broccoli and salsa; oil measured; no cheese. Overlaps in flavor with your Adobo Roasted Chicken & Potatoes but uses rice and broccoli.
